findings.description: The instance user_data embeds the RDS password (var.password) along with the DB endpoint, username, and database name, and writes them into a PHP include file on disk. EC2 user_data is stored in plaintext, is retrievable from instance metadata/console by anyone with instance-level access, and here the instance also carries a wildcard IAM policy, so credential disclosure is both persistent and high-impact.

The policy attached to catalog_app_role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", giving the workload full control of all S3, EC2, and RDS resources in the account. Because this role is assumed by the application EC2 instance, any compromise of that instance yields account-wide administrative-equivalent access and a straightforward privilege-escalation path.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS instance a public endpoint/IP. Even though the DB security group currently limits MySQL to the VPC CIDR, exposing a database to the public network removes a network boundary and means any future security-group or route change immediately exposes port 3306 to the internet.

storage_encrypted = false leaves the MySQL database, its automated snapshots, and its storage volumes unencrypted at rest, so anyone obtaining the underlying storage or snapshots can read the data directly.

The database security group allows all outbound traffic (protocol -1, ports 0-0) to 0.0.0.0/0. A database has no need for arbitrary internet egress; this permits data exfiltration and outbound command-and-control if the instance is compromised.

username = "admin" uses a predictable, well-known administrative account name, which aids credential-guessing and brute-force attempts against the database, particularly combined with its public accessibility.
